english: Guest, what is an elk? An elk is a great beast; it is bigger than a horse. Its horns are broad, and its legs are long. Do elks live here? They do not live here; they live by the cold lakes. How do you track them? We drive them into deep snow, and in it they do not run. May I see an elk!

pie: h₂énHe ḱléwse. gerh₂énes sréwmn̥ upér HrudHénti. h₁yód gerh₂énes gʷm̥yónti snóygʷʰos tinéh₁ti. suHnéwes moy súHn̥s h₂ew wrégōnti. h₁mé h₁éybʰi ḱóm sléh₂gʷonti? túH h₂yuHn̥ḱéh₂ h₁íns préḱsdʰi. h₁íns préḱsoh₂ h₁éysōm-kʷe dʰénwōr bʰoréyōh₂.
english: Grandmother, listen! The cranes are crying above the stream. When the cranes come, the snow melts. My sons will hunt the swine again. Will they take me with them? You are young; ask them. I shall ask them, and I shall carry their bows.

pie: eḱwos wewekur, "ḱludʰe, owei! ḱerd angʰetai widontbʰyos: ǵʰm̥on, potis, wl̥nam owiyōm kʷr̥neti soi gʷʰermom westrom; owibʰyos kʷe wl̥nā ne esti".
english: The horses said: "Listen, sheep, our hearts pain us when we see this: a man, the master, makes the wool of the sheep into a warm garment for himself. And the sheep has no wool."
